(b) THEN ONE Markdown table consistent with the Lock: - [Source Word] | [Morphology] | [Reference Equivalent] | [Contextual Definition] | [Grammatical Role] Source Text: 49 Ed una lupa, che di tutte brame 50 sembiava carca ne la sua magrezza, 51 e molte genti fé già viver grame, Reference Translation (provided): And a she-wolf, who with all cravings seemed laden in her meagreness, and already had made many folk to live forlorn,

**Interpretation Lock – FIRST (one bullet per source line)**
- **Line 49** *Ed una lupa, che di tutte brame* → *Ed* = additive conjunction “And”; *una* = indefinite article introducing a singular feminine noun; *lupa* = the female wolf, the referent of the clause; *che* = relative pronoun introducing a descriptive subordinate clause; *di* = preposition expressing accompaniment/association “with”; *tutte* = universal quantifier “all” modifying the following noun; *brame* = plural noun denoting “cravings, desires”.
- **Line 50** *sembiava carca ne la sua magrezza,* → *sembiava* = imperfect copular verb “seemed” (states a perceived condition); *carca* = adjectival predicate “laden, burdened”; *ne* = preposition “in” (locative/constitutive); *la* = definite article (here part of the possessive construction “la sua” = “her”); *sua* = possessive adjective “her”; *magrezza* = noun “meagreness, thinness”.
- **Line 51** *e molte genti fé già viver grame,* → *e* = additive conjunction “and”; *molte* = quantitative adjective “many”; *genti* = plural noun “folk, people”; *fé* = past‑remote of *fare* “made, caused”; *già* = temporal adverb “already”; *viver* = infinitive verb “to live”; *grame* = noun “grief, forlornness”, the state into which the folk are caused to live.
